column1: How is the load factor (alpha) calculated?
column2: It is the number of items stored divided by the number of buckets.

column1: Why are collisions inevitable in a hash table?
column2: There are more possible keys than buckets (the pigeonhole principle).

column1: How does linear probing handle a collision?
column2: It checks the next slot along and wraps around at the end of the array.

column1: What is the average lookup cost with chaining?
column2: O(1 + alpha), which stays O(1) while the load factor is bounded.

column1: Why does resizing rehash every key?
column2: Each key's slot depends on the table size; a new size means new slots.

column1: What is the worst-case cost of a hash table lookup?
column2: O(n), when every key lands in the same bucket.
